correctness.rationale: The period is exactly 2*3^(k-1) because 2 is primitive modulo 3^k. Every j-bit word is the floor image of a unit remainder. At j=m, missing bins are isolated multiples of three, permuted by M modulo Q; exact counting gives the floor formula. The positive-deficit phase and irrational-rotation densities follow with all boundary cases checked. Standard-library verification independently replayed 45,390 finite word-membership checks and 99 phase identities from the completed proof package. Finite checks are supportive only.

value.rationale: Complete sharp threshold and exact finite-level missing-word formula for a canonical arithmetic word family. Fixed-j convergence does not answer period-scale word universality. The nontrivial phase frequencies across exponents, including an irrational-rotation law, offer a structural explanation of why powers alternate between one-bit thresholds; this is not an arbitrary numerical special case.
